name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,123

clue.text: Excited cast use this in act

indicators.note: to cast metal is to pour it into a new shape, so the following words are remoulded

blocks.note: the four words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A director hopes a nervous cast will put real energy into the next act.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excited about a thing is eager and keen, full of zeal for it.

clue.text: Vacant setter brought up apathy regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means lifted from the bottom, so the word reads upward
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A setter with a blank mind was raised on a steady diet of indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant room or seat is unoccupied, containing nothing and nobody.

clue.text: Eel finally caught in net acted strangely like an octopus

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the eel
something caught in a net is trapped inside it
acting strangely means behaving oddly, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: its final letter
the letters of both words as fodder

explanation.surface: An eel trapped in a fishing net thrashes about like an octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus has eight long flexible arms, the feelers that make an animal so described.

clue.text: Troubled group of countries mostly appear in favour of board

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the United Nations
to come is to appear or arrive
being for something is supporting it
a board can mean a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: An international group struggles to show up and back the governing board.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling troubled means being uneasy, distressed or not at ease.

clue.text: Terrible cinema almost securing Odeon’s opening receipts

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes
securing means holding fast, so the jumbled letters enclose another
opening picks out the first letter of the cinema chain

blocks.note: the word without its final letter
the initial letter; Odeon is a British cinema chain

explanation.surface: A dreadful picture house nearly lands a premiere at the Odeon, the British cinema chain, and boosts its takings.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are money taken in, the earnings a business or person brings in.

clue.text: I envy cheaters, struggling with this?

definitions.text: I envy cheaters, struggling with this?

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing about, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the three words as fodder

explanation.surface: A faithful spouse admits envying people who stray, wondering if a restless phase is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone envious of adulterers may be suffering this restlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the supposed urge to be unfaithful after several years of marriage.

clue.text: Doctrine is meaningless to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with asks for just the starting letter of meaningless

blocks.note: taken as written
its initial letter

explanation.surface: A sceptic declares that a creed is pointless from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is a distinctive belief system, theory or ideology, often said dismissively.

clue.text: Child supporting university agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the child comes after

blocks.note: the common short form
a male child

explanation.surface: A child backs a college deal, as if parents and offspring reached a pact about tuition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in harmony or accord, everyone together.

clue.text: At first, pets are nervous in cat flap

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

blocks.note: the initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Household animals get jumpy when they have to go through the little door for the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat flap' reads as one thing, but the clue splits there: 'cat' ends the wordplay and 'flap' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is an informal noun for a state of agitated worry or alarm.

clue.text: Celebrity cleaner briefly recalled our distant relative

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the combined letters are taken back the other way

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity
a vacuum cleaner, shortened to the familiar abbreviation

explanation.surface: A famous cleaning personality is summoned back, though the clue then pretends to talk about family.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric humans are ancestors from long ago, hence a remote relation of modern people.

clue.text: Alternative to “aye”?

indicators.note: an alternative version of the quoted word is another arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: the quoted word taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the answer is an alternative way of voting yes, and an alternative order of the same three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary voting both words mean yes, so one can stand in place of the other.

clue.text: Messenger’s first warning to America of great significance

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the messenger

blocks.note: the initial letter
an omen is a warning sign
taken as written
the United States

explanation.surface: A courier brings a grave warning to the United States, a matter of real weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A momentous event is one of great importance or consequence.

clue.text: Grandiose dances arranged

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Elaborate, showy dances have been set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something organised has been set in order, planned or coordinated.

clue.text: Where you may find lag over instrument

blocks.note: a lag is British slang for a convict, found in a prison room
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to find something that is lagging behind an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' looks like a verb or pipe insulation; here it is an old convict, so the place is a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowed string instrument pitched below the viola is a member of the violin family.

clue.text: Extremely canny to welcome protest over humour

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, the outermost letters of canny
to welcome someone is to take them in, so the outer letters enclose the rest
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads upward

blocks.note: its first and last letters
a demonstration

explanation.surface: A shrewd person is wise to embrace a demonstration about jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment intended to amuse, the genre of being funny.

clue.text: The Spanish drink in Scottish town

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
a spirit

explanation.surface: A Spaniard has a drink while visiting a town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in Moray in north-east Scotland, known for its cathedral and whisky distilleries.

clue.text: Hot sweet bread with length removed

indicators.note: removed tells us one letter is taken away from the bread

blocks.note: a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A warm Christmas loaf has been cut shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' seems to describe the bread; it is slang for illicitly taken goods. STOLLEN has two Ls and one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot goods are slang for property recently obtained by theft.

clue.text: Intermediary seizing head of The Thinker

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the intermediary takes the next letter inside it
head of signals the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: a go-between in a dispute
its initial letter

explanation.surface: A go-between grabs hold of the famous Rodin sculpture of a seated figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thinker' looks like a title of the statue, but the wordplay takes only the first letter of 'The' and the definition is 'Thinker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who practises meditation is someone engaged in deep contemplation or reflection.

clue.text: Novel experienced in audiobook

indicators.note: an audiobook is listened to, so the word is judged by how it is heard

blocks.note: experienced in the sense of having known something; the silent K drops out when spoken

explanation.surface: A fiction book feels different when listened to as an audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' pretends to be a book; it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is original and unfamiliar, not seen before.

clue.text: Almost 168 hours plus 24 hours losing heart like a weakling

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped
losing heart means the central letter is taken away

blocks.note: seven days of 24 hours
one full day

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up a week and a day without a heart, a feeble specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A weedy person is thin and physically feeble, lacking strength.

clue.text: Unit went first, skirting black ice in retreat

indicators.note: skirting means running around the edge, so one piece goes either side of the rest
retreating moves backwards, so the assembled letters are read the other way

blocks.note: to lead is to go first
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off first, steering around a patch of black ice as they back away.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a logarithmic measure used for loudness of sound, one tenth of a bel.

clue.text: Tea dance using only one of its repeated parts

indicators.text: using only one of its repeated parts
indicators.note: the dance name is made of one syllable said twice, and we keep only one copy

blocks.note: the Latin American ballroom dance

explanation.surface: At a tea dance, a band plays only half of a repetitive tune.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea dance is an afternoon dance, but here 'Tea' is the definition alone; cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha, also spelt char, is informal British slang for a cup of the brewed drink.

clue.text: Where much is framed around second experience

indicators.note: around places the gallery on both sides of the following letter

blocks.note: the Tate is a London art gallery, full of framed pictures
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone describes a place where a lot of people have been wrongly set up, a second time round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' suggests a false accusation; here it means paintings in frames, pointing to a gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to undergo or sample it briefly, as in tasting freedom.

clue.text: With time running out, Italy hadn’t worked with EE

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deadline looms because the Italian side failed with the phone network EE.
explanation.walkthrough: EE is a British mobile phone network.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting when it is almost too late, with little opportunity remaining.
